records.english: Game Overview{LB}Sail the world's oceans with your companions.{LB}The world has seven regions. You lead a faction based in one of them.{LB}Each region has rival factions. Trade and battle your way to mastery of all seven seas.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Mysterious Token (Game Goal){LB}Rumor says a small item guides adventurers toward the Proof of Conquest. This item is known only as the Mysterious Token.{LB}No one yet knows its true nature or how it guides its owner.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Lure fleets{LB}Draw a rival fleet to a chosen city in the current sea region.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Bogus Documents{LB}Turn two rival factions against each other with forged orders. Select both targets.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Bad Rumors{LB}Spread rumors in one city.{LB}This reduces a rival's local share.{LB}A weak strategist may not devise this plot.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Bribery{LB}Bribe a broker to steal part of a rival's share. Choose one city in the current region.{LB}A weak strategist may not devise this plot.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Game Goal{LB}Each captain begins differently.{LB}[Raphael] Become a sailor.{LB}[Lil] Make money.{LB}[Hodram] Build the best navy.{LB}Every captain must collect seven Proofs of Conquest and rule the seas.{LB}{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Proof of Conquest{LB}Each sea has one treasure proving its owner's supremacy.{LB}Blind searching will fail. Gather information and clues around the world.{LB}Rumor says Mysterious Tokens guide worthy sailors to them.{LB}{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Choosing a Captain{LB}Three captains are available at first.{LB}Each has a different difficulty level and unique advantages:{LB}Raphael Castor{LB}Lil Argot{LB}Hodram Bergstrom{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Raphael Castor{LB}A Portuguese youth.{LB}inspired by Lisbon's sailors, he takes to sea.{LB}Many starting allies make him ideal for new players. Home: Lisbon.{LB}[1] Military investment costs 20% less.{LB}[2] Double power from ruins and items.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Lil Argot{LB}A Dutch merchant.{LB}She seeks a fortune in world trade.{LB}Little money and strong rivals make her route hard. Home: Amsterdam.{LB}[1] Sells goods for 5% more.{LB}[2] Double power from selling trends.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Hodram Bergstrom{LB}A Swedish admiral.{LB}He leads a poor navy toward world supremacy.{LB}He has good ships but strong rivals. Home: Stockholm.{LB}[1] Wins state rewards after battle.{LB}[2] Double power from victories.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Game Over{LB}The game ends if:{LB}1. Your share is zero in every city.{LB}2. Every ship is sunk or captured.{LB}3. Every ship has zero sailors.{LB}{LB}{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Tavern{LB}Recruit sailors and gather information.{LB}[Tip] Many Arab cities have no tavern. Replacing lost sailors can be hard, so battle carefully.{LB}Commands: Order Drink, Treat All,{LB}Recruit Sailors, and Plot.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Order Drink (Tavern){LB}A drink costs 5-10 coins. You may hear news about nearby cities or rival factions.{LB}[Tip] Large-city taverns have knowledgeable hosts. Speak with them often; they may even know where an item is hidden.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Treat Everyone (Tavern){LB}Buy drinks for everyone.{LB}Hear news about cities, rivals, or items. Doing this before recruiting attracts more sailors.{LB}{LB}{LB}{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Recruit Sailors (Tavern){LB}Hire crew. Developed cities offer more, but cost more. Excess crew are dismissed.{LB}Treating everyone first helps.{LB}Then use Assign Sailors to distribute them.{LB}{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Assign Sailors (Common Command){LB}Distribute crew among ships. Each shows Need, Now, and Max. Use Left or Right, or choose Auto.{LB}A ship below Need moves slowly.{LB}[flagship] fill it first.{LB}[even] equalize each ship's percent.{LB}[minimum] assign only Need.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Trade (Market){LB}Buy and sell goods where your faction has a share.{LB}Prices depend on city conditions. Your share and local stock limit purchases. Stock returns in its arrival month. High profit may reveal a Golden Route.{LB}[Tip] A purser may bargain or buy all stock.{LB}[Tip] Lil sells for 5% more.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Market info{LB}View prices and arrival months. Other cities cost 50-200 coins to inspect.{LB}Red prices mark fashionable goods.{LB}{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Trends (Market info){LB}Trending goods sell at much higher prices.{LB}Trends occur naturally or can be started by a missionary.{LB}Selling many trending goods may earn free share. in monopoly cities it may earn a Letter or Recommendation, which can unlock contracts.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Guild (Cities only){LB}Buy items, send diplomatic letters, and report Golden Routes.{LB}Ancient Maps are also sold here.{LB}{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Send Letter (Guild){LB}Send diplomacy to a faction in this sea.{LB}Requires an adjutant.{LB}Costs 1,000 coins and may fail.{LB}Unavailable if no rivals are present.{LB}Options: Goodwill, Alliance, Break Pact,{LB}Truce, Declare War, and Coerce.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Goodwill (Send Letter){LB}Send a friendly letter.{LB}Relations improve slightly.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Alliance (Send Letter){LB}Propose an alliance.{LB}Relations improve greatly and become Allied.{LB}Your ally may help in battle.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Break Pact (Send Letter){LB}End an alliance.{LB}Relations decline.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Truce (Send Letter){LB}Offer peace to a faction at war.{LB}War ends if accepted. Letters arriving during battle are discarded.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Declare War (Send Letter){LB}Declare war on another faction.{LB}Relations fall greatly and become At War. Their power appears red.{LB}[Tip] You may take an enemy's share through investment or battle.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Coerce (Send Letter){LB}Demand that another faction submit. Requires this sea's Proof of Conquest and an adjutant with 200 persuasion.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

inn{LB}Stay overnight.{LB}Each night costs one coin.{LB}Rest lowers sailor fatigue by about 10 and restores officers' health and HP.{LB}[Tip] A strategist may gather rival information. Press X to stop a long stay.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Palace / Governor{LB}Make contracts and military investments.{LB}Commands: Contract and Military invest,{LB}use Letter or Recommendation,{LB}Lend or Reclaim item.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Contract (Palace){LB}Make a contract with a city.{LB}Buy 1-20 units.{LB}Units grant city share and permission to trade.{LB}You cannot contract if three factions are present or rival shares already total 100%.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Military investment (Palace){LB}Buy 1-20 units of city defense. Each costs 50% of Arms; Raphael pays 40%.{LB}Arms rises. Your share may rise if total share is below 100% or an enemy owns share. High Arms resists attack and unlocks better ships and guns.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Use Letter (Palace){LB}Give a Market Letter to a ruler. Usable only in Port-size cities.{LB}Gain 5% share if contracted. Otherwise it creates a contract, taking 1% rival share even at 100%.{LB}Cannot be used with three factions present or when you own 100%.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Use Recommendation (Palace){LB}Give a Market Recommendation to a ruler in any city size.{LB}Gain 10% share if contracted. Otherwise it creates a contract, taking 1% rival share even at 100%.{LB}Cannot be used with three factions present or when you own 100%.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Lend item (Palace){LB}Lend an item to the ruler of your home city.{LB}Earn monthly rent based on value. Proofs of Conquest, Proof Maps, and Ancient Maps cannot be lent.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Reclaim item (Palace){LB}Retrieve a lent item at your home city's palace.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Square{LB}Gather news.{LB}Shops display signs here.{LB}Select a Trends sign to learn which goods are fashionable.{LB}You may Distribute Goods.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Distribute Goods (Square){LB}Give goods to residents for free. Requires a missionary.{LB}Those goods may become fashionable in nearby cities.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Shipyard{LB}Buy, modify, store, and repair ships; create or dismiss regional fleets.{LB}Work costs time and money. A shipwright may reduce the cost.{LB}Commands: Buy, Sell, Repair, Modify, and Dock.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Buy (Shipyard){LB}Available ship types vary by region.{LB}Name each ship after purchase.{LB}Choose Standard or Custom Order.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Standard Ship{LB}Buy a standard ship.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Custom Order (Buy){LB}Order a ship matching modifications on one you own.{LB}Only available where that ship type is sold.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Sell (Shipyard){LB}Sell a ship you own.{LB}sailors move to other fleet ships.{LB}Move its goods using Cargo Setup at the Port.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Repair (Shipyard){LB}Restore ship durability.{LB}Repairs cost money and take several days. A shipwright lowers the cost.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Modify (Shipyard){LB}Upgrade a ship.{LB}Choose Equipment or Rename.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Change Equipment (Modify){LB}Change or add ship equipment.{LB}Choose a location and press A to cycle choices.{LB}When all choices are ready, press Y to begin work.{LB}Options include sails, figurehead, extras,{LB}guns, holds, and cabins.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Change Sails (Modify){LB}Change a mast's sails.{LB}Square sails improve speed with the wind; lateen sails improve speed against it.{LB}Topsails help with the wind; staysails help against it.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
figurehead (Modify){LB}Mount a figurehead to protect the ship from some disasters.{LB}Requires an item in the figurehead category.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Extra Equipment (Modify){LB}Add or change armor, bow gear, or stern gear.{LB}Choose Armor, Bow, or Stern.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Armor (Extra Equipment){LB}Raises maximum durability but slightly lowers speed.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Bow Equipment{LB}Choose spritsail, bow gun, or ram.{LB}[Spritsail] More speed with the wind.{LB}[Bow gun] fire forward.{LB}[Ram] Strike enemy ships with the bow.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Stern Equipment{LB}Choose spanker or stern gun.{LB}[Spanker] More speed against the wind.{LB}[Stern gun] fire backward.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Change Guns (Modify){LB}Select the gun shown by the wheel to change its type.{LB}City Growth unlocks up to six gun types.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Holds (Modify){LB}Set holds as Marines, Gun Deck, Oars, Supplies, or Cargo. Oars cannot be added or changed.{LB}Some holds restrict use. Adding holds slows the ship. Maximum: four Marines, four Gun Decks, five Cargo; Supplies are unlimited.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Cabins (Modify){LB}Change officer cabins.{LB}Captain, Mate, Wheel, Survey, Lookout, Mast, and Deck cannot change type. Except for private cabins, masts, and decks, each cabin type is limited to one per ship.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Rename Ship{LB}Change a ship's name.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Dock (Shipyard){LB}Store or retrieve ships; manage regional fleets.{LB}Swap Ships, Appoint Captain, Arrange,{LB}Create regional fleet,{LB}Edit regional fleet,{LB}Dismiss regional fleet.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Swap Ships (Dock){LB}Store ships or retrieve them.{LB}Sailors, cargo, and supplies remain aboard.{LB}When retrieving, you may also Arrange and Assign Sailors.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Appoint Captain (Dock){LB}Assign an officer to each ship, including non-flagships.{LB}Cancel to use a common sailor. Assigning the hero makes that ship the flagship.{LB}[Tip] Captains gain levels faster.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Arrange (Dock){LB}Change ship order.{LB}The flagship is always first; choose the second, third, and later ships in order.{LB}Confirm after selecting every ship.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Create Regional fleet{LB}Create a delegated fleet.{LB}Choose a policy and an officer with Leadership 150 or more. Change policy with info.{LB}Each costs 100,000 operating coins; up to six fleets. if all ships sink, the officer returns.{LB}Policies: Delegate, Patrol, Dock, Attack.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Delegate Sea (Regional fleet){LB}Give the whole sea to its commander.{LB}The officer chooses trade and investment actions.{LB}A monthly balance report is sent.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Patrol (Regional fleet){LB}Wait near a contracted city and defend against rivals.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Dock (Regional fleet){LB}Dock at a contracted city.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Attack City (Regional fleet){LB}Attack an uncontracted city to reduce rival share.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Edit Regional fleet{LB}Change its ships while it is docked in your city.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Dismiss Regional fleet{LB}Dismiss it while docked in your city.{LB}its commander and remaining operating funds return to your fleet.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Port{LB}Load water and food, then sail.{LB}[Tip] if supplies are not full, the worker asks to resupply. Yes fills water and food evenly to maximum.{LB}No lets you adjust their ratio.{LB}Commands: Depart, Dock, Cargo Setup.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Depart (Port){LB}Begin a voyage.{LB}Choose Sail, Auto Move, or Deck View.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Sail (Depart){LB}Control the ship yourself.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Auto Move (Depart){LB}Travel automatically to a chosen city.{LB}Requires a captain and surveyor.{LB}Cities must share a route: the chart shows a line, and your faction has share at both ends and every stop. Valid routes appear red.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Deck View{LB}Same as common Deck View.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Dock (Port){LB}Same as the Shipyard Dock.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Cargo Setup (Port){LB}Move cargo among ships.{LB}Cargo left off every ship is discarded.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Ruins / Church (Cities){LB}Story progress may open a path to nearby ruins or churches.{LB}Discovering one raises faction power.{LB}Some offer rites or festivals that grant experience.{LB}[Tip] Ruins may hold rare items. Visit them.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
At-Sea Commands{LB}Commands available while sailing:{LB}Manual Movement,{LB}Auto Movement,{LB}info, Search, Declare War,{LB}Village and Battle,{LB}Sea Data,{LB}Common Commands.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Manual Movement{LB}Steer with the D-pad and turn sails with L/R. The touch screen also works. A/X changes sail spread.{LB}A: open sails and speed up.{LB}X: close sails and slow down. Half-open sails are automatic when every mast has a sailor.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Auto Movement{LB}The ship follows its route automatically.{LB}Press X to cancel and sail manually. Auto Move cannot restart at sea.{LB}[Tip] The Eagle Statue speeds time during Auto Move. Press A for normal time.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
info Mode (At Sea){LB}Press Y to pause and inspect cities and ships on screen.{LB}Search and Declare War begin from info Mode.{LB}Choose Search or Declare War.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Search Mode (At Sea){LB}Search around the ship.{LB}from info Mode press Y or R, then A to search.{LB}You may find water, food, or items. A failed search adds 3 fatigue and may cause desertion or animal attacks.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Declare War Mode{LB}Attack a ship or city on screen.{LB}from info Mode press Y twice or L, then select a target.{LB}Relations become At War and fall sharply.{LB}Attacking a city limits its commands.{LB}Allied fleets cannot be attacked.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Village{LB}Villages may be found while sailing.{LB}They may provide water, food, or repairs for a few coins.{LB}[Tip] Discovery reveals nearby land and sea on the chart.{LB}[Tip] Entering the promised password may start an event.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Battle{LB}Meeting an enemy or monster starts battle.{LB}You move ships as in manual sailing; guns and other attacks are automatic.{LB}See Battle Start, Victory, and Defeat,{LB}plus Battle Actions.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Battle Start{LB}Battle begins when:{LB}1. You meet a faction at war.{LB}2. You declare war on a fleet.{LB}3. A city attacks you, often near an enemy monopoly.{LB}4. A monster attacks.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Victory{LB}Meet one victory condition to end battle.{LB}Conditions depend on the enemy.{LB}See fleet Battle and City Battle,{LB}or Monster Battle.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Victory: fleet{LB}Win by reducing the enemy flagship's durability to zero,{LB}or capturing the enemy flagship.{LB}[Tip] Victory lowers enemy share in nearby cities. Captured ships may yield coins and cargo.{LB}{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Victory: City{LB}Win by reducing city Arms to zero,{LB}or making the city surrender.{LB}Low Arms makes surrender more likely.{LB}[Tip] Victory grants 10% city share.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Victory: Monster{LB}Defeat the monster. You may receive an item.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Defeat{LB}You lose when:{LB}1. Your flagship reaches zero durability, or 2. it is captured.{LB}[Tip] The hero moves to another ship and battle ends.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Battle Actions{LB}Attacks occur automatically.{LB}[Tip] Arrange officers for battle on Deck View beforehand.{LB}You may still rearrange after battle begins.{LB}Actions: Gunfire, Melee, Duel, Ram.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Gunfire{LB}Ships attack with mounted guns.{LB}More gun decks and stronger guns improve attacks. Bow and stern guns fire partly forward and back.{LB}[Tip] Put accurate officers on every gun deck for more shots.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Melee{LB}Sailors fight when ships touch.{LB}When the flagship touches an enemy, officers also fight and affect the sailors' result.{LB}[Tip] Put the hero in the captain's cabin and skilled fighters in Marines and on Deck.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Duel{LB}flagships may begin a duel when close.{LB}The boarding leader fights; without one, a deck officer or the hero fights.{LB}{LB}{PAD}
Ram Attack{LB}A ship with a ram may hole an enemy by striking its side.{LB}The target loses much durability; the attacker loses a little too.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Plot (Tavern){LB}Use a scheme against another faction.{LB}Requires an inspired strategist.{LB}Costs 1,000 coins and may fail.{LB}Unavailable without rivals. Except forged orders, you must have visited a city where the target owns share.{LB}Options: Lure, forged Orders, Rumors, Bribe.{LB}{LB}{PAD}

Report Golden Route (Guild){LB}Report a Golden Route you discovered.{LB}Receive discovery rewards for a limited time.{LB}Each route can be reported only once.{LB}See Golden Route Log and Discovery.{LB}{LB}{LB}{LB}{PAD}
